title: Rockfall and Explosion at Halema`uma`u Crater
place: Halemaʻumaʻu lava lake, Kīlauea summit, Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park
audio: source audio kept (AAC) - not listened to
notes: SPARE, LOW RES (640x480 source with black border; picture only x~0.12-0.88,y~0.0-0.75 of frame). Daytime webcam: 0-2.5 s crater wall + small lava lake; ~2.5-3 s rockfall from the left wall -> dark explosion cloud with orange spatter (x~0.3,y~0.5), then a white/brown plume fills the left half. Webcam timestamp text top-left (y<0.04) and a USGS bug below the picture - crop away.
fact_en: Rocks falling into the summit lava lake generated an explosion that threw large fragments of molten lava onto the rim of Halema‘uma‘u Crater, 85 m (280 ft) above the lake.
